findings.reason: without a planted not-produced source and a deliberately truncated archive, neither gate can show it fires, and §4's planted-source control is the model the other two sections should follow.
findings.text: §2's done-when offers only regression guards (export gate 0, sourceless drafts not rising) for a measure that is a read-back count, so a read-back that counted attempted instead of produced sources would pass it; §3 line 48 likewise names an integrity test of the whole stream with no control showing that a truncated or corrupt copy fails it

findings.reason: the control needs its execution mode stated, or meeting it leaves a planted source in the population the census reconciles, which is the defect class this plan's own guards exist to prevent.
findings.text: §4's control "a source planted outside every class makes them disagree" reads as a write into the live source population, and the plan does not say it is planted in a disposable graph and retracted, on a repository that spent several sections recovering stray and sourceless live sources

findings.reason: a done-when whose output has no named durable location cannot be checked by a later reader, and this is the one line the author can add without touching any mechanism.
findings.text: the §4 done-when requires a re-run census whose class sums reconcile and spend recorded beside the remaining cap, but names no path for either, and §2 line 43 refers to "the cohort's committed read-back" without one, so the evidence can land in a run directory rather than in docs/evidence/fragments/ as the parent §52 required

response_events.note: §2 now requires the read-back to report a source planted as attempted-but-not-produced in a disposable graph as not produced; §3 requires the integrity test to fail on a deliberately truncated copy of the archive.
